framework.summary: The bill requires developers to write no safety framework or plan.

transparency_report.summary: No public report is required; the Energy program gives test reports only to participating developers.

incident_reporting.summary: Developers have no duty to report incidents to a government body.

imminent_risk_reporting.summary: The bill sets no shorter window for imminent-risk incidents.

third_party_audit.summary: Developers must take part in the Energy Department's testing program, which uses independent third-party assessments only to the extent feasible; no private audit is required.
third_party_audit.quote: to the extent feasible, establish and facilitate classified, independent third-party assessments and blind model evaluations

whistleblower.summary: The bill has no employee protections.

registration.summary: No registration or licensing; developers must take part in the federal evaluation program and may not deploy without complying.

shutdown.summary: The Energy program must only develop recommended containment protocols; developers have no duty to build a shutdown capability.
shutdown.quote: develop recommended containment protocols, contingency planning, and mitigation strategies informed by testing data to address identified risks

compute_threshold.summary: An advanced AI system is one trained with more than 10^26 operations; the Secretary may propose a new definition only if Congress approves by joint resolution.
compute_threshold.quote: trained using a quantity of computing power greater than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations

revenue_threshold.summary: Coverage does not depend on revenue, spending or users.

harm_threshold.summary: Adverse incidents are defined by type of event, with no death, injury or damage figures.

penalties.summary: A person who violates the participation or deployment rules is fined at least $1,000,000 per day of violation; the bill does not name an enforcer.
penalties.quote: shall be fined not less than $1,000,000 per day of the violation

effective_date.summary: The bill states no effective date; it sets deadlines counted from enactment.

notes: No enforcer named for the penalty. Deadlines run from enactment (program in 90 days, plan in 360 days, sunset 7 years); no effective-date clause.
